explanation: It began in Ouagadougou. Its top prize, the Golden Stallion of Yennenga, honours a legendary warrior princess said to be the mother of the Mossi people.

claims.text: FESPACO was first held in 1969 in Ouagadougou, in the country that is Burkina Faso (then Upper Volta).
FESPACO did not begin in Senegal, Mali or Cameroon.
The festival's top prize, the Golden Stallion of Yennenga, is named after a legendary princess.
In legend, the warrior princess Yennenga is the mother of the Mossi people.

writerNotes: Upper Volta stays out of player text on purpose: p.hist.0156 asks which country was called Upper Volta, and C22 pairs the two items on their shared answer. Related, not the same fact. Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor; the schema's riskReason list has no only or counterintuitive, so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: mledoze-countries (cca3=BFA) and geonames-cities (Ouagadougou, BF) place Ouagadougou in Burkina Faso; the 1969 founding needs web evidence. Rival test: Senegal, Mali and Cameroon are French-speaking West and Central African countries with strong film traditions (Ousmane Sembène was Senegalese), so each tempts. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: an African festival; the French acronym and the options give reasoners a foothold. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 26 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json, no match. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: the festival became biennial only later, so the stem says first held in 1969 and avoids every two years.

evidence.restatement: The festival that became FESPACO was first held in Ouagadougou, in Upper Volta (Burkina Faso since 1984), in 1969.
